newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent drifts sideways as market takes breather.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent drifts sideways as market takes breather.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures drifted sideways in mid-afternoon trade as the market took a breather after Monday's huge gains.
"The whole board is taking a rest. It could be preparing for another move up but at the moment things are pretty slack," said one broker.
Feb Brent was trading six cents up at $24.62 a barrel at 1541 GMT, having just dipped briefly into the red.
Brokers said that the whole complex was dominated by the weather and moves on NYMEX heating oil.
"Heat is having a small correction after yesterday but we could see some positive numbers again," said a dealer.
Independent forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Tuesday that temperatures have been above normal over the last 24 hours in the Northeastern United States, the world's key heating oil market.
But temperatures are expected to dip below normal today and fall to 3-6 degrees Fahrenheit (2-3 Celsius) below normal on Wednesday.
The next resistance for Feb Brent was seen at Monday's high of $24.73 a barrel, while support was at $24.48.
Jan gas oil was trading $1.75 a tonne down at $230.25 a tonne at 1541 GMT, off the session low of $228.50.
The downward move was partly in response to difficulty in moving physical material in inland Europe because of icebound canals, brokers said.
The front month backwardation eased 75 cents on the day as traders roll forward their positions ahead of the Friday expiry of the Jan contract.
